lines.en: Okay.
I’m tired of winter.
And I would very much like summer to come back now.
I wonder if Maya knows any way to sort of just...push up the date of the next reset and usher in another change of seasons or something.
The cold was nice at first- but even now, in the earliest stages of its death, I grow tired of its tomfoolery.
Desperate for a change of pace, I clutch my fists together and wait for Maya to conveniently appear before me.
Everyone knows that once I think of something like that, it almost always immediately happens. And I see no purpose in a reversal of fortune this early on a Monday morning.
: Any minute now.
: Hey! Crazy seeing you here, Sensei.
: Hey, Maya. You got exponentially taller, tanner, and less weird since I last saw you.
: Maya? Are you wandering around looking for her or something?
: It’s more like I’m...wandering around in search of summer. And Maya is the only person I know with time manipulation powers.
: You know, I always thought there was something weird going on with her, but time manipulation was pretty low on my list.
: Well, now that you know, I’m excited for you to either forget all about it or just think I’m joking.
: Oh, come on. If superpowers like that were real, Chinami would be like, flying around and killing dragons or whatever it is wizards actually do.
: Fantasy isn’t my favorite genre, so I'm not going to pretend to know much about it, but I’m pretty sure wizards don’t fly.
: So, is this just what you’re doing for lunch? Walking around, fantasizing about Maya instead of your real girlfriend?
: This is actually one of the very rare occasions where I’m not fantasizing about something that would make you mad at me.
: Wait, what is that supposed to mean?! How often are you fantasizing about stuff like that?!
: Sorry, did I say stuff that would make you mad at me? I meant...fantasizing about the two of us on some sort of romantic getaway or...some other cute thing.
: Aww~ You’re so sweet. This is why I love you.

Every day I spend with Chika is one day closer to realizing that she lives in a world of blissful ignorance, where only the things she wants to hear manage to stick to whatever part of the brain stores memories.
Which is great for me, don’t get me wrong. But being that far into dreamland might be a little dangerous, especially when it comes time for her to leave.
She...has to realize eventually, doesn’t she?
That even on the days where I want this to be anything more than it is, there’s another side of me buried somewhere in the back of my head mocking me for even pretending it’s real.
I just don’t want to be the one to force her into realizing that it’s not...and that this relationship was all built on one huge misunderstanding.
A misunderstanding that is, of course, my fault. And I’m an idiot for thinking that even a teenager as mature as Chika would think like an adult 100%% of the time.
But I really can’t just let this go on forever.
: Wanna go have sex in your office?
A little longer wouldn’t hurt, though.
: Yes.
: Too bad. I’m hungry.
I hate girls.
: Hey, wanna come with me to the cafeteria? We can eat lunch together and no one will think it’s weird because you’re a teacher.
: I think me doing things like this is exactly why there are so many rumors apparently spreading about me.
: Yeah, but those are just rumors. Rumors are always going to exist, Sensei.
: Like that one about you dating Niki Nakayama. Like, obviously that never actually happened, but people are still saying it.
: That did actually happen, though.
: Hahah~! Sure it did, Sensei.
: Before I offer to call her and prove you wrong, will you tell me why you don’t think it’s true? Am I not cool enough to date an idol?
: I think you’re the coolest guy in the world. And one of the hottest, too.
: One of?
: Idols are on another level, though. Especially ones like Niki. They don’t date anyone because they belong to all of us.
Boy, do I have bad news for her.
: This was before she became an idol, though.
: Well, she wasn’t Niki before she became an idol. She was just Niki.
: Oh, okay. My mistake. I didn’t realize she was possessed by the soul of music.
: Well, I’m glad I got to be the one to educate you for once.
: When have I ever educated-
: Now, come with me to the cafeteria and eat lunch with me like the awesome, loving, loyal boyfriend you are.
: You know, I’m not really feeling that hungry today.
: Well, I am. So that sucks for you.
: I’m sorry?
: Because you’re coming with me whether you like it or not.
: I don’t think this is how relationships are supposed to work.
: It’s exactly how they’re supposed to work. Besides, it’s not like anybody is going to come up to us and tell us to like, not eat together or something.
: We’re not doing anything wrong. We’re just...making the most of our lunch period since we’re not always able to spend time together, you know?
I...guess this could be a good time to talk to her about this whole “dating” thing?
Especially now that she’s trying to act like we’re dating in[school], which is exactly what I wanted to avoid at all costs.
And something I thought she’d care a little more about avoiding too, but...it is what it is.
: Fine.
: But I’m not paying for your food since I’m already paying for your phone bill.
: Yeah, yeah. I can buy my own food. I’m a big girl.
Chika tries to grab my hand to lead me down the hall, but I am able to dodge her grasp and inform her that holding hands is a little too much.
And by a little, I mean a lot.
It’s not like we’re in the lobby of a hotel or a private onsen or anything like that. There are people here.
There are times when it’s okay to be clingy and times when it’s not.
And while the two of us are fully clothed and out in the open, I’d say the current status of acceptability is far closer to not.
So, the good thing is that the cafeteria is mostly empty today.
The bad thing is that a few of the people who are here are people that I know.
No one “dangerous” like Ami or Noriko or...anyone else who would get mad at me for sitting with a girl who isn’t them.
But there's Yasu, Touka, that one new teacher, and Io- all the way back in the corner of the room, doing her best to assume the role of a socially anxious wallflower.
And, even though I can’t see her from where I’m sitting, I’m sure she’s thinking something along the lines of, “Oh, good. They’re still together,” while, unbeknownst to everyone but me, we’re not.
: You sure you’re not hungry? Because I probably won’t finish all of this and you can have whatever’s left of it.
: I’m okay. Ami made a big breakfast this morning.
: But, Ami makes a big breakfast pretty much every morning, so that’s nothing to really write home about.
: Yeah...that’s actually super impressive. Like, doesn’t she leave the dorms really early every morning just so she can go home and cook for you? That’s some serious dedication.
: Yeah, but I let her live in my house for free, so there’s that too.
: Aren’t you also her legal guardian?
: I prefer the term “uncle.”
: Okay, but aren’t you like, legally her legal guardian?
: You’re sure talking a lot for someone who was very hungry just a moment ago.
: All I’m saying is that she...really goes out of her way for you.
: It kinda makes me a little jealous.
: Like...I want to cook breakfast for you and like, help out around your house and stuff.
: One key difference between you and Ami is that Ami doesn’t have to also take care of a kid. Just me.
: Though, I guess there is Ayane sometimes, and she can be a bit of a handful.
: Your house sounds really...lively.
: Sometimes, yeah. Most of the time, it’s just me and her, though.
: I really hate to ask like this...but...
: When I’m like, out of [high_school] and stuff...
: Do you think there’s any chance that maybe Chinami and I could move in with you?
: Like, you won’t have to hide how we’re seeing each other anymore once I’m not a student, and it would definitely help me out since I wouldn’t have to worry about rent anymore.
: What about Yumi? Where will she go?
: I don’t know. I’m sure she doesn’t expect me to take care of her forever, though. Like...she’s going to have to find something to do on her own.
: And it’s not like I’m going to ask you if she can just come live with us as well when you haven’t even agreed to my sister and me coming yet.
: I’d...have to run it by Ami.
: Is Ami not leaving for college once she’s out of high school? Is all of that stuff she says about just devoting her entire life to you really true?
: Or do you think maybe she’s just saying that for now and...she’ll change her mind once it’s time to start like, growing up?
: I think that you probably shouldn’t think too much about things that will be happening three years from now when we don’t even know what’s going to happen tomorrow.
: Yeah? Are you gonna run off with my favorite idol and forget all about me?
: Cause I wouldn’t really blame you. There’s no way I could compete with her.
: At the risk of shattering your borderline inhuman expectations of Niki, I’m going to tell you now that she’s probably...not what you think she is.
: Yeah, because I’m sure you know her so, so well.
: Well, considering that she is my ex-girlfriend I think it’s safe to say I know her at least a little well.
Just...only the tsundere parts. Not the ones Niki so desperately wants me to remember.
: Sensei, I’m not going to believe that! Are you and Noriko working together to spread this rumor or something?
: Because if I believe this one, I’ll have to start believing the ones about how you’re secretly seeing like half of our class. Or how you and Maya-
: Wait, weren’t you looking for Maya when I bumped into you in the hall?
: Nope. But back to the topic of Niki, we really did date in high school.
: Yeah, okay. I mean, I obviously don’t have a problem with it, but aren’t you in your thirties? How would you have dated Niki in high school if she’s like, ten years younger than you?
: Chika, just out of curiosity, how old do you think Niki is?
: She’s 22 and her birthday is March 3rd. Her favorite color is pink (Shocker, I know) and if she could live anywhere in the world, it would be Hawaii.
: And where did you get that information?
: Fan books...online...interviews. The info is all over the place, Sensei. At least do your research before trying to make me think you dated my role model.
Well, if nothing else, Niki was certainly right about the idol industry being ruthless and cutthroat.
I’ll have to add this newfound revelation to the exposé I’m writing.
: Chika, Niki is 29 years old. Only a couple years younger than me.
: Oh, please. She’s 29 and she still looks like that? Funny joke, Sensei.
: Besides, if I ever found out that my lips have been on the same penis as Niki's, I’d probably bite it off out of excitement.
: Sensei, come on! I’m obviously joking!
: Chika, there are certain things in life that you really just shouldn’t joke about...and biting someone’s penis off is one of them.
: Don’t worry. I like your penis too much to bite it off.
: I am very relieved to hear that. Now, if only you’d stop acting like that during the day at school.
: What do you mean?
: Just that this was supposed to be a little more secretive than eating lunch together and trying to hold my hand in the hallway.
: Well, gee. Sorry for being in love with you. I don’t really see what the big deal is.
: The “big deal” is that you could get me in trouble.
: You could get both of us in trouble.
: And if you’re not going to respect that-
: Wait....Are you breaking up with me?...
: Woah, hold on a second.
: Why?
: What did I do wrong?
: Is this because I asked to move in with you after [high_school]?
: You can say no! I didn’t mean to move so fast!
: Oh god, no. I really wasn't trying to-
: Chika, calm down.
: I'm sorry.
: I just thought that you were about to give me like...an ultimatum or whatever...
: Then it clicked that I just asked about moving and...
: Are we okay?...
: We won’t be if you don’t stop crying.
: People are going to start thinking something is going on which, need I remind you, is exactly what I’m trying to avoid.
: But we can forget about that for now...
: You still haven’t eaten. Your food is going to get cold.
: Yeah.
: I’m...suddenly not very hungry anymore...
The rest of the lunch period goes by in mostly silence as I realize how foolish I was for even thinking that now would be a good time to tell Chika to tone it down.
And, at this point, I’ll be lucky if any time winds up being a good time to tell her that.
The worst part is that I want to blame her for all of it.
I want to blame her for misunderstanding what I wanted out of our time together...and painting me into a portrait of the family she’s always wanted.
I’m the one who handed her the brush, though. And blaming her for using it just makes me question why I ever gave it to her in the first place.
She loves that portrait so much, though. So how am I supposed to tell her I hate it?
It doesn’t matter now, I guess.
I’ll just keep putting it off.
The same way I've been doing from the start.
But, hey. At least on the bright side-
I’m one day closer to summer.
Chika’s affection has increased to [chika_love]!
